effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the new text (DB2-EN101, Dark Beginning 2)

transitions.historical_text: When this card is Summoned (excluding Special Summoned), destroy 1 face-up Dragon-Type monster on the field.
transitions.modern_text: When this card is Normal Summoned or Flip Summoned, destroy 1 face-up Dragon-Type monster on the field.
transitions.summary: Wording clarification only: 'When this card is Summoned (excluding Special Summoned)' (TP2-002) became 'When this card is Normal Summoned or Flip Summoned' (DB2-EN101), which names the same two summon events - the modern script encodes exactly those, one mandatory targeting Trigger Effect on EVENT_SUMMON_SUCCESS cloned onto EVENT_FLIP_SUMMON_SUCCESS. No resolution changes, so no historical implementation is needed for either period snapshot.

review.notes: Conflicting evidence, escalate. The variant's cdb text ('When a "Dragon Seeker" is changed to Attack Position: You can target 1 face-up Dragon-Type monster on the field; destroy it.') matches no lineage version (best match v1 at ratio 0.6036), and its script matches that text rather than the printed one: EVENT_CHANGE_POS with a previous-position-Defense / now-Attack condition, optional instead of mandatory, and requiring an existing valid target (Duel.IsExistingTarget) where the modern mandatory version activates regardless ('if chk==0 then return true end'). It also borrows its effect description from an unrelated card id (aux.Stringid(276357,0) is 'Shinobird Salvation'), which suggests a hand-rolled entry rather than a maintained period reconstruction. Card data is identical to modern (2000/2100, Level 6, DARK, Fiend), so the script is the only difference. Whether upstream encoded an OCG-original trigger - and if so when the TCG version diverged - cannot be settled from this packet; the English lineage's only transition is the cosmetic clarification recorded above, and no chronology for a position-change trigger exists here, so nothing is dated for it. Note also that the GOAT snapshot (2005-04-01) predates DB2-EN101 (2005-07-27), so a GOAT-era Dragon Seeker displays the TP2 text while behaving identically.
